subject.title: [Feature]: Pluggable STT backend for macOS Push-to-Talk

question: Should native macOS Push-to-Talk gain a batch STT backend seam, and should that seam reuse `tools.media.audio`, Talk transcription providers, or a new native-only contract?
rationale: The code confirms the missing capability, but the safe implementation depends on product and security choices about microphone audio routing, credential handling, fallback behavior, private-network access, and whether this belongs in native app code or existing provider/plugin contracts.

options.title: Design native PTT batch seam
options.body: Keep Apple Speech as the default, add a final-text batch backend boundary for PTT, and route provider choice through the existing media/provider security model where possible.

options.title: Route through existing provider/plugin surfaces only
options.body: Treat this as plugin/provider work unless a missing generic native-app extension API is identified, avoiding a macOS-only config surface in core.

options.title: Defer custom STT for native PTT
options.body: Keep current Apple Speech-only native PTT behavior until privacy, fallback, and endpoint policy are settled.

recommendation.title: Design native PTT batch seam
recommendation.body: Keep Apple Speech as the default, add a final-text batch backend boundary for PTT, and route provider choice through the existing media/provider security model where possible.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved decision is centered on the native macOS PTT pipeline, where steipete has the strongest sampled history signal.
